recommendation: Keep the empty audit commit as-is. No further core FHIR source change is recommended for FHIR-23920 unless BR&R makes a new decision to reverse the later Ingredient link-direction model.
issue_request: FHIR-23920 asked how to express ingredients for a simple single-part MedicinalProductDefinition without being forced through PackagedProductDefinition and ManufacturedItemDefinition details such as package type, package quantity, and manufactured dose form. The final Published/Persuasive with Modification resolution said this had been improved, with Jira comments identifying MedicinalProductDefinition.ingredient as the simplification.
initial_application: No source commit explicitly tagged FHIR-23920 was found. Current source nevertheless contains MedicinalProductDefinition.ingredient as an active 0..* element and includes a simple MedicinalProductDefinition example with inline ingredient values; history shows this was introduced and refined through the broader R5 medication-definition resource work rather than an issue-tagged FHIR-23920 commit.
additional_context: MedicinalProductDefinition and Ingredient are active BR&R resources in source/fhir.ini. FHIR-28584 first moved the medication-definition model toward CodeableReference for simple code-or-resource use, and the later Published FHIR-31808 reversed Ingredient link direction so current MedicinalProductDefinition.ingredient is a CodeableConcept shortcut while full Ingredient resources point back through Ingredient.for. FHIR-26989 separately addressed the mandatory manufactured-dose-form burden and is already represented on the combined branch.
reconciliation: No source change was made. Current source already lets implementers express simple product ingredients directly on MedicinalProductDefinition as codes, or associate full Ingredient resources with the product via Ingredient.for when more detail is required. Reintroducing a direct MedicinalProductDefinition-to-Ingredient reference would conflict with the later Published link-direction decision.
